record: National Historic Landmark documentation, Lapham–Patterson House, 70000868
facts: Three-story Victorian mansion. The front combines two octagonal bays with an inset polygonal porch, turned brackets, a narrow second balcony, and a north porte-cochère. The back has two long wings and stained glass.

record: Georgia Department of Natural Resources architectural history, pp. 155–158
facts: The upper-room turret and main porch share a projecting hood. Several compound gables join above the U-shaped plan. The house has three decorative chimneys, one split into two flues, and wood siding in several patterns.

record: Digital Library of Georgia exterior catalog text
facts: Pale yellow Victorian house with red fish-scale shingling and a two-story porch with two supporting posts. Source used as a written color and form description.
